note: Monday 21 Sep 2026 ~07:02 SGT run, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00 / HKEX 09:30; JPX additionally closed today for a bank holiday). No new cash market session since Friday 18 Sep. 6 of 14 items are from the last 24-48h (Sun 20/Mon 21 Sep). UPDATE vs Sunday's file: Trump's posture on the Houthi/Aramco crisis has hardened -- he reportedly cut a Camp David trip short and is weighing a 'large-scale' military response, a more active stance than Sunday's flat rebuff. Also new: Aramco's crude cuts now extend into October with Dated Brent reportedly topping $130 as displaced Gulf barrels reroute to Asia; HKMA hiked in lockstep with the Fed; crypto's own Fear&Greed gauge (71, Greed) is diverging sharply from CNN's equity gauge (still ~26-29, Fear); and gold is holding firm despite the hawkish Fed hike. The exact CNN Fear&Greed component breakdown remains unavailable -- its site/API are still blocked -- so market.json's fearGreed block carries the same caveat.

items.headline: Trump cuts Camp David trip short, weighs 'large-scale' military response after Riyadh strike
items.summary: Trump returned to the White House early Saturday night and is reportedly deliberating a major strike on Houthi/Iran-linked targets ahead of a Tuesday Gulf-leaders meeting, telling reporters 'anything could happen with me.' This is a more active posture than Friday's dismissive 'fine and dandy' comment, even as he has still declined a direct Saudi request for US strikes.
items.actionable: Escalation risk now cuts both ways -- a US strike could restore confidence and cap the oil/miners hedge, or trigger Iranian retaliation across the Strait of Hormuz and extend it; don't reduce the precious-metals sleeve into this binary.

items.headline: Aramco cancels all Sept/Oct European crude allocations; Dated Brent tops $130 as Gulf exports redirect to Asia
items.summary: Saudi Aramco has zeroed out October term deliveries to at least two European refiners on top of the September cancellations, after Houthi/Iran-linked strikes forced the 4-million-bpd East-West pipeline offline. Roughly 1-1.5mn bpd of displaced Saudi Gulf-side barrels are being rerouted to China, Korea, India and Japan instead; a sharply higher Dated Brent print was reported by one secondary source this run but could not be reconciled against the tracked futures series, so no specific Brent level is asserted here.
items.actionable: The supply cut is deepening in duration, not just September -- reinforces holding the precious-metals/miners hedge through month-end even though WTI futures themselves fell on Sunday's reopen (see model.json for the reconciliation).

items.headline: Sept 23-24 Xi-Trump White House summit teeters on $14bn Taiwan arms-sale dispute
items.summary: Xi Jinping is due in Washington Sept 23-24, but Beijing has warned via diplomatic channels it will cancel the summit if Washington approves a pending $14 billion Taiwan arms package (F-16 upgrades, air-defense, anti-ship missiles) before his arrival. A senior US official disputed that characterization, but the dispute remains unresolved with days to go.
items.actionable: Binary catalyst for HK tech this week: a completed summit with a trade/rare-earth truce would be a strong bullish trigger for Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi; a cancellation would hit them hard -- consider trimming size or hedging ahead of the summit rather than after.

items.headline: Taiwan tracks 20 PLA aircraft, 14 ships as President Lai inspects precision-strike drill
items.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry reported tracking 20 Chinese military aircraft and 14 vessels around the island Saturday, deploying its own missile systems in response, while a Chinese reconnaissance drone was spotted off Taitung. President Lai Ching-te visited Pingtung County the same day to inspect a live-fire drill of the armed forces' precision-strike capability.
items.actionable: Cross-strait friction is running hot right as the Xi-Trump summit approaches; keep position sizing on Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi mindful of headline risk into this week.

items.headline: HKMA hikes base rate 25bp to 4.25% in lockstep with the Fed
items.summary: Hong Kong Monetary Authority's currency-board mechanism forced an automatic follow-on hike after the Fed's Sept 16 move, raising HIBOR-linked borrowing costs across HK's pegged-currency market.
items.actionable: Adds to the S-REIT/HK-property financing-cost headwind and extends similar pressure to HK banks; reinforces caution on SGX REIT and HK property adds into Q4.

items.headline: Bitcoin pushes to ~$81,300 on record ETF inflows, decoupling from macro headwinds
items.summary: Bitcoin traded between $81,280 and $81,300 Saturday, up roughly 4% from Friday's ~$77,900 print, on substantial net inflows into US spot BTC ETFs and a fresh mining-difficulty record. The move came despite Treasury yields pushing back toward 5.00%, suggesting crypto flows are trading on their own momentum rather than rate expectations.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio holding, but the BTC melt-up is a useful read-through for overall risk appetite/liquidity conditions heading into the new week.

items.headline: Crypto Fear & Greed hits 71 (Greed), up from 61 a week ago -- diverging sharply from equities' Fear reading
items.summary: alternative.me's crypto Fear & Greed index has risen through the weekend to 71 (Greed) even as CNN's equity gauge sits in Fear (~26-29, CNN's own site/API remain blocked to direct fetch), with Bitcoin holding in the high-$70s/low-$80s on continued ETF inflows.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio holding, but the widening sentiment gap (crypto greedy, equities fearful) is worth watching -- if it reflects genuine risk-on liquidity it could presage stabilization in HK tech/SGX by midweek; if it's crypto-idiosyncratic, don't read it through to equities.

items.headline: Fed's Warsh cryptic 'dose of accommodation' remark stokes October hike speculation as Fear & Greed slips to Fear
items.summary: Following the Sept 16 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's abbreviated press conference featured a widely-parsed 'dose of accommodation' comment that Wall Street is reading as leaving the door open to another hike in October. CNN's Fear & Greed index slipped into Fear territory (reports range 26-33 across trackers, CNN's own site remains blocked) on the hike, even as the S&P/Nasdaq closed the week near record highs.
items.actionable: Keep an eye on October Fed pricing -- a hawkish surprise would pressure the large cash pile's opportunity cost narrative and could cap silver/gold upside near-term even amid geopolitical support.

items.headline: Silver near $66.50/oz amid sixth straight annual physical deficit forecast
items.summary: Silver traded around $66.51/oz Friday, up 2% on the day though roughly flat over the past month, still 54% higher year-on-year. The physical market is on track for a sixth consecutive annual deficit, forecast at 46.3 million ounces for 2026, even as a stronger dollar post-Fed-hike has capped near-term gains.
items.actionable: The structural physical deficit remains the core long-term bull case for the levered silver/miner sleeve, independent of near-term dollar strength from the Fed hike.

items.headline: Gold holds near $4,383/oz, extending post-Fed-hike resilience
items.summary: Gold has pushed back toward its recent highs for a second straight session even after the Sept 16 hawkish Fed hike, an unusual divergence (gold normally weakens on hikes) attributed to a combination of record central-bank buying and the Gulf oil-shock's safe-haven bid outweighing rate-driven dollar strength.
items.actionable: Gold shrugging off a hawkish Fed while a live Mideast supply shock unfolds is a strong signal to hold, not trim, the gold/miners sleeve into the new week.

items.headline: MP Materials draws fresh analyst attention despite premium valuation concerns
items.summary: Jefferies reiterated a Buy rating on MP Materials with a price target well above current trading levels, and William Blair added MP to its September Analyst Conviction List citing expected higher rare-earth production and expanding magnet output, even as the stock has seen profit-taking since a September 9 investor day offered no major new catalysts. MP posted a 12th straight quarterly operating loss despite 89% revenue growth. Separately, China's own suspension of its October-2025 rare-earth export controls is set to expire 2026-11-10 -- a concrete second date for the whole ex-China basket (MP, Lynas, Energy Fuels, USA Rare Earth) to watch alongside this week's Xi-Trump summit.
items.actionable: Valuation is stretched (premium multiple, continued losses) even as the strategic bull case (government-backed capacity, China export leverage) stays intact -- both Sept 23-24 and Nov 10 are now dates to track before adding to the rare-earth watchlist.

items.headline: SMIC slides 3.76% as chip stocks lag; Tencent, Xiaomi hold up
items.summary: SMIC (0981.HK) fell 3.76% to HK$73.00 as semiconductor names came under pressure, while Tencent (0700.HK) edged up about 1% and Xiaomi (1810.HK) closed HK$26.40, up nearly 1%. The divergence suggests rotation within HK tech away from chip-cycle-sensitive names ahead of the Xi-Trump summit.
items.actionable: SMIC's underperformance versus Tencent/Xiaomi argues for watching relative positioning within the HK tech sleeve rather than treating it as a single bloc into the summit.
